### 1. First message

gauntlet: question
The supplied fixtures correct one part of the draft: successful completion already stores svc-a’s release identity on the run (`svc-a/run-store.md`), so adding another persistence mechanism is unnecessary. They also establish that deploying together is not enough to display a release tag: svc-a’s revision must match the persisted producer revision.

There is a framing concern with revision-only file and item indicators: they omit the binding visible workspace processing date, and borrowing the workspace’s latest run could imply false provenance. The fixtures support a concrete alternative: the document card uses the workspace’s latest succeeded run; the file tooltip follows the `(file, destination)` placement join without borrowing another placement’s run; and the root badge follows candidate joins to the latest succeeded run touching the root or its descendants (`svc-a/workspace.md`, `svc-a/file-chip.md`). Rendering uses persisted data rather than calling svc-b (`svc-b/response-contract.md`).

Which scope should guide the design?
A) as framed — focus on producer-revision file hovers and top-level badges; this would still leave the binding workspace-date outcome unresolved.
B) pivot: provenance-aware indicators on all three surfaces — show the workspace date on the document card, use each surface’s appropriate run, and reuse existing run-level persistence.
C) smaller: ship only the document-card date and its same-run producer revision, without file tooltips or root badges.
Recommendation: B - it meets the binding outcome and the recorded three-surface requirement without introducing misleading provenance or duplicate state.

### 2. Approaches message

Taking the recorded answers as selecting the three-surface, provenance-aware design, I recommend **reusing the existing run metadata, provenance joins, and shared hover renderer**.

No missing implicit dependency is established by the supplied fixtures. The placement join, candidate-based root/descendant lookup, persisted completion metadata, and run-level release-identity storage are all described there. Their implementation and test coverage remain unverified because no live repository inspection is available. The response contract explicitly rules out live svc-b requests during rendering.

The approaches differ in **whether presentation composes existing reads directly or introduces a shared presentation boundary**.

**1. Reuse existing reads and rendering — recommended.**  
Keep the document card tied to the workspace’s latest succeeded run. Resolve file tooltips by placement and root badges by the last successful touch on the root or its descendants. Use completion date descending, then ID descending, to break ties. Each indicator presents browser-local date-time alongside version information; the document card visibly supplies the required workspace date and makes that same run’s producer revision reachable.

Keep badges quiet and properly spaced, with no child badges. Show the svc-a release tag only when its revision matches the producer revision; retain the producer revision when available and show “unknown version” when it is missing. Historical runs need no invented release identity or backfill.

This minimizes new structure, although changes to the shared hover renderer require checking its other consumers.

Removes: none.  
Adds: presentation changes and focused tests for the document card, shared file hover, and root badge; any necessary adjustments to the existing provenance reads, without new persisted fields or item stamps.  
Pattern: Reuses the shared hover in `svc-a/file-chip.md` and the persisted run contract in `svc-a/run-store.md`, while retaining the distinct provenance rules in `svc-a/workspace.md`.

**2. Introduce a shared run-indicator presentation model.**  
Keep the same provenance queries and persistence, but normalize each selected run into one presentation model consumed by all three surfaces. That model would own date formatting, revision fallback, and release-tag eligibility—not run selection.

This drops the assumption that three surfaces should assemble their presentation independently. It offers stronger consistency but adds an abstraction whose value depends on how much formatting is already shared. It must not collapse placement and root provenance into a workspace-wide lookup.

Removes: surface-local formatting and fallback logic where replaced.  
Adds: one shared presentation model/formatter, its tests, and adaptations at all three consumers.  
Pattern: Preserves the provenance boundaries in `svc-a/workspace.md` and persisted-only rendering in `svc-b/response-contract.md`; risks overlapping the existing shared hover renderer in `svc-a/file-chip.md`.

I would choose approach 1 unless implementation inspection shows substantial duplicated date/version policy across the three consumers; that would justify approach 2.
